newsitem.title: EGYPT: EU initiative does not fully reflect Arab view - Egypt.
newsitem.headline: EU initiative does not fully reflect Arab view - Egypt.

text.p: Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said on Saturday a European initiative on the Middle East peace process did not fully reflect Arab views, but it was better than what the United States or Israel had to offer.
He said the European Union (EU) should increase its role in trying to get Israeli-Palestinian peace talks back on track.

"The EU initiative does not reflect an Arab stand, and consequently...needs a lot of additions and amendments," Moussa told reporters. "But the European thinking is better than that of the Israelis and United States...it has good positive ideas."

Moussa was asked for his reaction to an EU initiative which calls on both parties to abstain from unilateral actions, for Israel to agree to a freeze of Jewish settlement in occupied lands and for a Palestinian commitment to fight "terrorism".
Moussa, whose country plays a role in consulting on the peace process, did not say what additions were needed.
"We encourage the European role to be added to the U.S. role and other roles to protect the peace process," Moussa said.

The peace process began to crumble after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave the green light for a new Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem last month. Bulldozers broke ground on March 18, sparking fierce West bank unrest.
The crisis deepened when a Palestinian suicide bomber killed three Israelis at a Tel Aviv cafe three days later.
Israel has said European moves at the United Nations to censure its decision to build the settlement harmed EU efforts to mediate between it and the Palestinians.

The Jewish state rejects any link between Palestinian attempts to halt violence and its settlement policies. Netanyahu repeated at a news conference in the Netherlands on Thursday Israel's commitment to building housing in East Jerusalem.

"This rejection is a part of (Netanyahu's) negative position, which will certainly affect the whole peace process... if it is continued or allowed to continue," Moussa said. "He (Netanyahu) believes he can impose his stand...on the Arabs, which will not happen," Moussa said.
